title: The Slow Mirror
summary: Ben buys an old mirror from a shop on Saturday.
coverScene: A cozy bedroom at night with a large, beautifully designed wooden mirror reflecting a young man who is standing perfectly still.

sentences.text: Ben had always loved old things.
Therefore, he spent his Saturdays exploring the old shops in town.
One afternoon of rain, he discovered a beautiful mirror.
It had a heavy wood frame with strange patterns.
The glass was perfect and showed no signs of age.
It seemed to shine even in the dark corner.
If I had more money, I would buy that table too, Ben said quietly.
However, the mirror was very cheap.
He paid the owner immediately and carried it home.
He hung it on the wall opposite his bed.
It quickly made the whole bedroom look much larger.
That night, Ben was washing his face before bed.
He looked into the mirror to check his image.
He raised his hand to touch his mouth.
Suddenly, he felt a strange, cold wind pass.
He stared at his image in the glass.
He thought he saw a slight delay in his movement.
It seemed that the image moved just a bit after him.
He shook his head and laughed quietly at his own thoughts.
He decided that he was simply tired from work.
If he went to sleep early, he would not think about such things.
The next morning, the delay was a clear reality.
It was no longer just a mistake of his tired mind.
When Ben waved his hand, the image waited.
The image only started to wave after Ben stopped.
He stood frozen in front of the glass.
He watched his own face smile back at him three seconds late.
He has never seen such a strange thing before.
He felt very afraid of this strange sight.
However, he was also very interested in this impossible physical thing.
He spent an hour testing the mirror.
He walked back and forth, and each time the image followed slowly.
He wanted to tell his friends, but he was afraid.
They might think he was not right in his mind.
During the next week, the delay grew much longer.
By Wednesday, the image was nearly ten seconds behind his actions.
He would sit at his desk to read a book.
Meanwhile, his image was still standing near the door.
The mirror was slowly becoming a window into a past moment.
This made Ben feel very worried in his bedroom.
He tried to cover the glass with a thick sheet.
However, he felt a strong urge to keep watching it.
It was like a dangerous game that he could not stop playing.
One evening, Ben noticed that the image had a different attitude.
He was looking down at his phone.
Suddenly, he felt a clear feeling of being watched.
He quickly looked up at the mirror.
However, the image was still looking down at the phone.
A few seconds later, the image raised its head.
Its eyes locked onto Ben with a cold stare.
It smiled a smile that was wider than any smile Ben ever gave.
He wanted to return the mirror immediately, but the shop was closed.
That night, a terrible storm began.
The sound of heavy rain beat loudly against his bedroom window.
Ben lay in bed, unable to sleep.
He stared at the dark frame of the mirror across the room.
The weak light from the street lights cast long, moving shadows.
Suddenly, he decided to end this strange situation.
He wanted to break the mirror with a heavy chair.
He stood up and walked slowly to the center of the room.
He stopped directly in front of the glass.
The image was still lying in bed with its eyes closed.
The image did not know that Ben had moved.
Ben stood perfectly still and held his breath.
He waited to see how long it would take to catch up.
After ten seconds, the image slowly opened its eyes.
It sat up on the edge of the bed.
It looked around the reflected room.
Then, it turned its head to look directly at the real Ben.
The image did something that made Ben's heart freeze with fear.
It stood up, but it did not walk toward the glass.
Instead, it turned its back and walked toward the door.
Ben tried to move his arms, but his body was completely frozen.
He was unable to make any sound.
He watched with fear as his image opened the bedroom door.
The image stepped out into the dark hall in the glass.
As the image left, the real bedroom became very dark.
Soon, the room was in a deep, heavy dark.
Ben was left standing alone in the cold silence.
He was unable to turn his head or close his burning eyes.
He realized that he no longer controlled his own physical life.
He was now just an image kept in the mirror.
He must always wait for a master who will never return.
If only he had never bought that terrible mirror.
He would still be free in his own home.

sentences.text: Ben had always loved old things, which was why he spent his Saturdays exploring the dusty shops in town.
One rainy afternoon, he discovered a beautiful mirror with a heavy wooden frame that was designed with strange patterns.
The glass was perfect, showing no signs of age, and it seemed to shine even in the dark corner of the shop.
"If I had more money, I would buy that whole table too," Ben whispered to himself, admiring the fine craft.
However, the mirror was surprisingly cheap, so he paid the owner immediately and carried his new possession home.
He hung it on the wall opposite his bed, where it quickly made the entire bedroom look much larger.
That night, as Ben was brushing his teeth before bed, he looked into the mirror to check his reflection.
As he raised his hand to wipe his mouth, he felt a strange feeling, like a cold wind passing.
He stared at his image, and for a brief moment, he thought he saw a slight delay in his movement.
It was as if the person in the glass was reacting just a tiny bit after him.
He shook his head, laughing quietly at his own imagination, and decided that he was simply tired from work.
If he had gone to sleep earlier, he would not have imagined such a silly thing.
The next morning, the delay was no longer a trick of his tired mind, but a clear reality.
When Ben waved his hand, the reflection waited until he had completely finished the movement before it began to wave.
He stood frozen in front of the glass, watching his own face smile back at him three seconds late.
It was a deeply disturbing sight, yet he was also fascinated by this impossible physical phenomenon.
He spent an hour testing the mirror, walking back and forth, and each time the reflection followed slowly behind.
Although he wanted to tell his friends about it, he was afraid that they would think he was crazy.
During the following week, the delay between Ben and his reflection grew longer and more obvious.
By Wednesday, the image in the mirror was nearly ten seconds behind his actual physical actions.
He would sit at his desk to read a book, and the reflection would still be standing near the door.
The mirror was slowly becoming a window into a past moment, which made Ben feel very uncomfortable in his bedroom.
He tried to cover the glass with a thick sheet, but he felt an odd urge to keep watching it.
It was like a game that he could not stop playing, even though the stakes felt increasingly dangerous.
One evening, Ben noticed that the reflection was not just slow, but it also seemed to have a different attitude.
While Ben was looking down at his phone, he felt the distinct feeling of being watched by his own eyes.
He quickly looked up, but the reflection was still busy looking down at the phone in the glass.
A few seconds later, the reflection finally raised its head, and its eyes locked onto Ben with a cold stare.
The smile on the reflected face was slightly wider than any smile Ben had ever given in his life.
If he could have returned the mirror to the shop, he would have done so immediately, but the shop was closed.
That night, a terrible storm began, and the sound of heavy rain beat loudly against his bedroom window.
Ben lay in bed, unable to sleep, staring at the dark frame of the mirror across the quiet room.
The pale light from the street lights outside cast long, moving shadows that danced across the wooden floor.
Suddenly, he decided to end this mystery once and for all by breaking the mirror with a heavy chair.
He stood up from his bed, walked slowly to the center of the room, and stopped directly in front of it.
The reflection was still lying in the bed, its eyes closed, completely unaware that Ben had moved.
Ben stood perfectly still, holding his breath, waiting to see how long it would take for his image to catch up.
After ten seconds, the reflection in the mirror slowly opened its eyes and sat up on the edge of the bed.
It looked around the reflected room, and then it turned its head to look directly at the real Ben standing there.
Instead of walking forward to match Ben’s position, the reflection did something that made Ben’s heart freeze with absolute fear.
It stood up, but it did not walk toward the glass; instead, it turned its back and walked toward the door.
Ben tried to move his arms, but he realized that his own body was completely frozen, unable to make any sound.
He watched with fear as his reflection opened the bedroom door in the mirror and stepped out into the dark hall.
As the reflection left the room, the lights in the real bedroom began to fade into a deep, heavy darkness.
Ben was left standing alone in the cold silence, unable to turn his head or even close his burning eyes.
He realized then that he was no longer the person who controlled his own physical life in the real world.
He was now just a trapped image, waiting forever for a master who would never return to the glass.
If only he had never bought that beautiful, terrible mirror, he would still be free in his own home.

sentences.text: Ben had always felt a quiet reverence for objects that had survived the passage of time, and that reverence guided his Saturday wanderings through the town's forgotten shops.
The air inside those cramped rooms was thick with the scent of old wood, dust, and the faint perfume of forgotten lives.
Shelves bowed under the weight of tarnished silverware, cracked porcelain, and yellowed books whose pages whispered stories to anyone who listened.
Ben moved slowly, his fingertips brushing the surfaces as if seeking approval from the ghosts of the past.
Each discovery felt like a secret handshake between him and history, a promise that the old would not be forgotten.
One drizzling afternoon, a low-pitched rain tapped the shop's window, and Ben's gaze fell upon a mirror framed in heavy oak etched with bewildering arabesques.
The glass itself was startlingly clear, reflecting the dim bulb above without a single flaw, as if it held its own private light.
"If I had more money, I would buy the whole table as well," Ben whispered, admiring the craftsmanship that seemed to echo centuries of hand-work.
To his surprise, the proprietor offered the mirror for a fraction of its apparent value, and Ben handed over the cash without hesitation.
He lugged the heavy frame home, then positioned it opposite his bed, where its presence instantly expanded the cramped bedroom into a broader, uncanny space.
Later that night, Ben stood before the sink, toothbrush in hand, and glanced at his reflection as he brushed away the day's fatigue.
As he lifted his hand to wipe his mouth, a sudden chill brushed his neck, as though a cold draft slipped through an invisible crack.
For a fleeting instant, the image in the glass seemed to lag, its movements arriving a fraction of a second after his own.
Ben chuckled softly, convincing himself that exhaustion had conjured the illusion, and he turned away, convinced the mind could play tricks in the dark.
He promised himself that an earlier bedtime would banish such fanciful thoughts, never suspecting the mirror had already begun to rewrite reality.
When dawn painted the walls with pale gold, Ben approached the mirror once more, this time with a skeptical smile.
He raised his hand in a casual wave, and the reflection obeyed only after he had completed the motion, its motion delayed by three heartbeats.
The sight of his own face smiling three seconds later sent a shiver down his spine, a mixture of dread and fascinated curiosity.
Over the next hour he paced back and forth, testing the mirror with every deliberate step, each movement echoed after a growing pause.
Though he longed to share the phenomenon with friends, the fear of being dismissed as mad kept his discovery locked behind the glass.
Throughout the following week the lag widened, each day adding a little more time between his actions and their mirrored echo.
By Wednesday the reflection was almost ten seconds behind, a ghostly lag that turned his bedroom into a theater of delayed performances.
He would sit at his desk to read, and the image in the glass would still be lingering near the doorway, unaware of his current presence.
Even when he covered the glass with a thick sheet of cloth, an inexplicable compulsion urged him to lift the veil and watch the slow dance once more.
The mirror had become a silent opponent in a game he could not quit, its stakes growing more unsettling with each passing hour.
One evening, as Ben scrolled through his phone, he sensed an unfamiliar weight in his own gaze, a feeling that his eyes were being watched.
He glanced up, only to find his reflection still hunched over the device, oblivious to his sudden attention.
Moments later the mirrored figure lifted its head, and its eyes locked onto Ben with a cold, unblinking stare that seemed to pierce his soul.
The smile that spread across the reflected face was unnaturally broad, wider than any grin Ben had ever managed in his own life.
He wished he could return the mirror to the shop, but the shutters were closed, sealing his curiosity within the darkened room.
A fierce storm rolled in that night, hurling sheets of rain against the bedroom window like relentless drummers.
Streetlights flickered, casting long, wavering shadows across the wooden floor, each movement echoing the slow pulse of the mirror's secret.
Ben lay awake, his heart hammering, eyes fixed on the dark frame that seemed to breathe with an unseen life.
Determined to end the mystery, he fetched a sturdy wooden chair, intending to shatter the glass with a single, decisive blow.
He rose from the bed, each step echoing on the floorboards, and positioned himself directly in front of the mirror, his breath held like a held note.
The reflected Ben lay still in the bed, eyes closed, as if unaware that his counterpart had risen and approached.
Ben stood perfectly still, his muscles tensed, waiting to see how long the delayed image would take to catch up.
Ten seconds slipped by, each tick of the clock sounding louder than the rain, until finally the reflection's eyelids fluttered open.
It sat up slowly, surveyed the mirrored room with a detached curiosity, then turned its head directly toward the real Ben.
Instead of moving forward to meet him, the image rose, turned its back to the glass, and walked toward the doorway as if fleeing.
When Ben attempted to raise his arms, an invisible force held his limbs in place, and not a single sound escaped his throat.
He watched, helpless, as his reflection opened the mirrored bedroom door and stepped out into a darkness that seemed deeper than the night outside.
As the reflected figure vanished beyond the threshold, the lights in Ben's actual room dimmed, swallowing the space in a suffocating blackness.
He felt his own eyes burn, his body unable to turn, his mind trapped in a silent scream that echoed nowhere.
In that moment he understood that he was no longer the master of his own flesh, but merely an image awaiting a master who would never return.
The realization crashed over him like a wave of cold iron, and regret settled in his chest like a stone.
He imagined the shopkeeper's warm smile, the polished wood, and the moment he first set eyes on the glass, now a portal of dread.
If only he had walked away, the room would have remained a simple bedroom, its shadows harmless and its walls ordinary.
Instead, he was bound to the slow, unyielding rhythm of a mirror that refused to reflect the present, forever pulling him into its past.
The storm raged on outside, but inside the only sound was the silent tick of time that no longer belonged to Ben.
